item.title: LLM Inference at Scale: vLLM and llm-d on Kubernetes
item.description: Running AI infrastructure breaks a lot of the traditional ways we’re used to dealing with systems. In this blog, I write about how you can serve AI models efficiently for inference on Kubernetes on hardware like GPUs (which are super expensive!!!), and how vLLM can help you manage memory efficiently while llm-d can help load balance the system smartly to your needs.

item.title: MCP Doesn't Make Your Model Smarter, It Makes It Capable
item.description: This is my first post in my “Today I Learned” series. Words like MCP host, MCP server, protocol, agent, subagent, tool, and RAG get thrown around so easily as buzzwords. I tried to put together a simple explanation of them so that anyone can understand it.

item.title: About Me
item.description: Hi, I am Kashish. I am a third year Computer Science student, based in Toronto, Canada. I am starting to build a habit of writing down what I learn as I learn it. I came across Simon Willison’s TIL, and inspired by that I am starting my own “Today I Learned” series where I’ll put up what I just figured out, and maybe you find them useful too :) and also I can look back at them later and remember what I learned and how far I have come.
